subject: BUG: Can't use a \ref{} in a fig.cap

messages.author: 467324c7303934a0
messages.subject: BUG: Can't use a \ref{} in a fig.cap
parts:
Using: 
knitr_1.4.1, R 3.0.1:


The following document fails to compile with pdflatex, when a \ref{} is included in a fig cap='' string.
The bug, as shown below the document is that the computed fig.scap is missing a closing } in the
\ref string.

% !Rnw weave = knitr
\documentclass{article}

<<knitr-setup, include=FALSE>>=
options(width=70)
opts_chunk$set(fig.align='center', fig.height=6, fig.width=7, fig.pos='hbt!')
opts_chunk$set(out.width = '.6\\linewidth')
@

\begin{document}
Testing fig ref in a fig caption...

Plot one figure...

<<fig1, fig.cap='Plot of \\texttt{1:10}'>>=
plot(1:10)
@
Then, refer to it in another...

<<fig2, fig.cap='The same plot shown in Figure \\ref{fig:fig1}'>>=
plot(1:10)
@

Result:  File ended while scanning use of \texttt{\@caption}!

\end{document}

What is generated in the .tex document clearly shows that the scap has been truncated at the ':'
and therefore is missing the closing '}'

\caption[The same plot shown in Figure \ref{fig]{The same plot shown in Figure \ref{fig:fig1}\label{fig:fig2}}
\end{figure}

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] BUG: Can't use a \ref{} in a fig.cap
parts:
It is a known issue, and I do not know how to solve it automatically:
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/18958063/latex-error-with-fig-cap-in-knitr-and-sweave

You can either suppress the short caption by fig.scap=NA or "", or
overwrite it like fig.scap="a custom short caption"

Regards,
Yihui

messages.author: 467324c7303934a0
messages.subject: Re: BUG: Can't use a \ref{} in a fig.cap
parts:
This bug is actually more general than I thought.  In my example, it was triggered by the \texttt{1:10}
in fig1, and thus all fig.cap containing some Latex code are prone to this error in the
composing of the fig.scap.

The work-around for now is to use fig.scap='' whenever you use Latex code withing a fig.cap.
The following now works:

% !Rnw weave = knitr
\documentclass{article}

<<knitr-setup, include=FALSE>>=
options(width=70)
opts_chunk$set(fig.align='center', fig.height=6, fig.width=7, fig.pos='hbt!')
opts_chunk$set(out.width = '.6\\linewidth')

@

\begin{document}
Testing fig ref in a fig caption...

Plot one figure...

plot(1:10)
@
Then, refer to it in another...

<<fig2, fig.cap='The same plot shown in Figure \\ref{fig:fig1}', fig.scap=''>>=
plot(1:10)
@
\end{document}

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Re: BUG: Can't use a \ref{} in a fig.cap
parts:
It is triggered by ":", because the default value for fig.scap is the
character string before ",", ".", or ":" in fig.cap. In your cases, I
cannot just truncate the string at the colon, since that will lead to
an incomplete LaTeX expression.

Regards,
Yihui
